newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan coffee stocks seen at low levels until 1997.
newsitem.headline: Japan coffee stocks seen at low levels until 1997.

text.p: Japan's coffee stocks are likely to remain insufficient until early 1997, as local roasters, expecting world bean prices to drop further, continue to trim purchases, traders said on Wednesday.

Local warehouse stocks of coffee at the end of October totalled 64,833 tonnes, down 18.8 percent from 79,857 tonnes a year earlier, the Agriculture Ministry said. The figure was 83,428 tonnes in August 1995.
Japan is the world's number-three coffee consumer after the United States and Germany.

"The October stock figure is equivalent to Japanese coffee consumption for about two months. This is certainly below sufficient inventory levels," a coffee trader at a major trade house in Tokyo said.
Traders attribute the lower stocks to limited buying by domestic roasters, which expect world coffee prices to drop further.
Japanese roasters usually buy coffee for April to May shipment at this time of the year, but they are still trying to cover February to March, traders said.
"We're recommending that roasters step up buying because of falling domestic stocks. But they're still hesitating to return to the market," another coffee trader said.
"Local coffee stocks are likely to remain low until early next year," he said.
A decline in coffee imports last year was also behind the lower stocks, traders said.

Japan's coffee imports in calendar 1995 reached 299,555 tonnes, down 13 percent from 344,635 tonnes in 1994, Finance Ministry data showed. Bean imports from Brazil dropped by 12 percent to 68,748 tonnes during that period.

"The volatile yen/dollar rate last year and serious frost damage to Brazilian coffee made Japanese roasters nervous and hesitant to buy actively," said Masao Yamashita, executive director of the All Japan Coffee Association.
"Coffee stocks have fallen below sufficient levels, partly because of the import cuts last year," he said.
Total green coffee imports of Japan in the first 10 months of 1996 were 276,072 tonnes against 263,700 tonnes in the same period of the previous year, ministry data showed.
